Commentary.Commentary: That's all we have from this fascinating Test match but this multi-format series isn't over yet. Australia Women lead India Women 6-4. The action now switches to the T20Is and the first of three matches will be played on October 7th. The match will start at 6.40 pm local (8.40 am GMT) but the coverage will begin sooner. Do join us for that one. Till then goodbye and take care.

Australia Women skipper, Meg Lanning says, that they had to fight it out and is proud of the group. Mentions that without the weather they would have got a result. Tells that they certainly came to win and so did India. Credits India for playing so well and putting them on the back foot.

India Women captain, Mithali Raj says, that if they would have got four odd wickets then they would have gone for a few more overs. Mentions that Jhulan Goswami has been their best bowler over the years and they got to see why she is the best.  Adds that they do have quite young talents on their side and she is impressed by Yastika Bhatia and how Richa Ghosh played in the ODIs. Mentions that Jhulan's experience came in handy as young seamers, Pooja Vastrakar and Meghna Singh were given an opportunity to learn from her. Ends by saying that she is sure that Harmanpreet will take the field in T20Is.

PLAYER OF THE MATCH, Smriti Mandhana says, that the ton was definitely one of the top highlights for her. Mentions that she is happy that she passed those tough phases of the 80s and 90s and got to that hundred and was lucky with that no ball on 80, as that cleared her mind and wanted to make it count. Tells that to have two or three slips, a gully only happens in Test cricket and to play this historic Test is a great feeling as they were playing the Day-Night Test for the first time. Adds that they don't have much time as they move forward to the T20I series and have about three days to rest.

After the dinner break, India Women came out for their second innings and the onus was on Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma to score quickly but Ellyse Perry and Darcie Brown bogged them down for a bit. The India Women openers did start motoring along and went past yet another half-century partnership. Just when Smriti Mandhana looked in full flow, Sophie Molineux sent her back to the pavilion and Ashleigh Gardner got rid of the dangerous Yastika Bhatia soon after. This put the brakes on the India Women innings for a while. Mithali Raj didn't declare when the tea break took place and Shafali Verma, along Punam Raut came out to bat. Verma brought up a half-century and Raj did finally declare with the lead being stretched to 271 runs. With just 32 overs remaining in the day's play, it was always going to be tough for either team to force a result. Jhulan Goswami and Pooja Vastrakar did provide a couple of breakthroughs for India Women but the Aussie skipper, Meg Lanning ensured that no further wickets fell. With just one hour remaining the two captains decide to shake hands and this historic Test match came to an end as both teams shared 2 points each. A draw was maybe a fair result but India Women were ahead throughout most of this match and have shown that they are on par with the Australia Women team in all aspects.

The outcome was not the one both groups of supporters were looking for but it is a result that will please the neutrals. Apart from the result, everyone will be happy with how the match was played. We saw more than a full day washed out due to severe weather conditions and still, the match was absolutely gripping till the end. India Women played beautifully with the bat in the first innings and put up a huge total of 377/8 on the back of a brilliant ton from Smriti Mandhana and a gritty half-century from Deepti Sharma down the order. Others chipped in as well but India Women bowled equally well and didn't give an inch to Australia Women batters in that first innings. Ellyse Perry and Ashleigh Gardner were the heroes for Australia Women with the bat as both notched up half-centuries, helping their team avoid the follow-on. India Women had a lead of 136 runs as Meg Lanning decided to declare with Australia Women on 242 for 9, which was a very sporting decision trying to force a result.

Well, well. The umpires signal for DRINKS but Mithali Raj is having a discussion with her team. Meg Lanning is also seen having a word with the India Women skipper. Mithali Raj finally gives her decision and she's content with a DRAW. So, the historic pink-ball Test comes to a premature end and the result no one wished for but looked the most likely is the final outcome. The game was not moving at a rapid pace in this final session and the decision to shake hands seems a logical one. So, both teams get 2 points added on and the T20Is will now decide the series.
Tosses it up, outside off. Perry lunges forward and blocks it out.
On middle, blocked out.
Short and outside off, Perry chops it back towards slip.
Full and outside off, Perry steps out and drills it to cover.
This one is pushed quicker and Perry is pushed on the back foot. Perry looks to flick but misses and gets hit on the pads. A huge appeal but turned down. Maybe an inside edge as well.
Gaikwad sees Perry charging down the track and fires it in at the toes. Perry bunts it back to the bowler.
A length ball, on top of off. Lanning taps it to point. A maiden from Pooja Vastrakar.
Pitched up, outside off and this one seams back in off the surface. Lanning makes an easy leave.
Back of a length, around off. Meg Lanning rocks back and taps it to point.
Full and straight, well kept out by Lanning.
Length again, this time its on middle and angling in. Lanning defends it out.
A length ball, outside off. Lanning lets it through to the keeper.
Very full, on off and kept out by Perry.
On middle and leg, Lanning works it to mid-wicket for a single.
Flatter one, on off. Lanning nudges it towards point.
Gaikwad gives this one some air and Perry dances down the track. She flicks it towards square leg and they get a single.
A tad bit short and cut away to point.
Nicely tossed up, around off. Perry strides forward to defend but gets hit on the pads. Rajeshwari Gayakwad appeals but the umpire remains unmoved.
Time for some spin now! Rajeshwari Gayakwad comes into the attack.
Pitched up, on middle. Lanning defends it off the front foot.
Length again, angled in at middle and leg. Lanning keeps it out on the leg side.
Length ball, around off and shaping away a bit. Lanning leaves it alone.

FOUR! A short ball now, on off stump. This one doesn't rise enough and Meg Lanning gets right on top of the bounce. Lanning pulls it with authority and the ball races into the vacant mid-wicket fence.
A touch fuller, on middle. Lanning pushes it firmly to mid on.
Length ball, on off. Lanning stays solid in defense.
Full and around off. Perry drives it to cover.
Back of a length, on off. Perry blocks it out.
Fullish ball, on off. Perry presses forward and drives it to mid off.
Full and wide outside off. Perry leaves it alone.

LEG BYE! Lovely delivery from Jhulan Goswami. This one is on a length on off and the ball seams in off the surface. Lanning looks to block but the ball goes through bat and pad, past the slip cordon. The visitors appeal for an LBW but turned down. They get a leg bye. Now, was there any edge on it?
Pitched up, on off. Lanning defends it out.
Full and on the pads, Lanning flicks it to deep square leg for a single.
Ellyse Perry comes in at number 4.

OUT! CAUGHT! Pooja Vastrakar strikes for India Women! She bangs a short ball, on middle. Beth Mooney looks to pull but can't get on top of the bounce. The ball goes off the top edge and skies up towards deep square leg. Rajeshwari Gayakwad runs ahead and grabs the catch with both hands. Australia Women lose their second wicket and Beth Mooney will have to walk back to the pavilion.
Commentary.Howout: c Rajeshwari Gayakwad b Pooja Vastrakar

On the pads, Mooney tucks it to deep square leg for a run.
Short ball, on off. Mooney watches the ball and lets it sail through.
Length ball, around off. Mooney prods and drives it to mid off.
On a length, outside off. Lanning punches it towards covers.
Ohhh! That one keeps a bit low! Length ball on middle, Lanning does well to bring her bat down in time.
On a good length on off, blocked out.
FOUR! That's a lovely shot! Full and outside off, Meg Lanning lunges forward and steers it through backward point for a boundary.
Length ball, outside off. Left alone.
Good-length ball on middle, nipping back in. Lanning blocks it out with a dead bat.
Good-length ball, around off. Mooney pushes it to mid off.
On off, Lanning pushes it towards covers and takes a single.
Good-length ball on middle, defended towards covers.
Fuller in length, on off. Mooney steps out and drives it towards covers for a single.
Short of a length, outside off. Mooney leaves it for the keeper to collect.
Full and outside off, Mooney shoulders arms to that one.
Outside off, Lanning lets it sail through.
Length ball on off, jagging back in. Lanning looks to push it on the off side but inside-edges it onto the pads. Goswami pleads the umpire for an LBW but there was a clear inside edge there.
On a good length on off, Lanning covers the line and defends it out.
Good-length ball, on off. Lanning puts a stride forward and looks to defend but the ball goes off the outside edge towards first slip.
Good-length ball on middle, blocked right under eyes.
On a length, on middle, Lanning nudges it to mid on.
Full and outside off, Mooney defends it back down the track.
FOUR! What a shot! Length ball, outside off. Beth Mooney leans and creams it through covers for a boundary.
Good-length ball around off, Mooney looks to drive but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Good-length ball, outside off. Mooney leaves it alone.
Full again, outside off. Pushed to mid off.
Fuller in length, outside off. Mooney pushes it to mid off.
Here comes the first change. Pooja Vastrakar comes in to replace Meghna Singh.
Well bowled and well kept out by Lanning. On off and nips back in off the surface, keeping a bit low. Lanning gets her bat right behind the line.
Good-length ball, around off and Lanning taps it off the back foot through point. She picks up a brace.
Pitched up, outside off. Lanning shoulders arms.
Right on the money from Goswami. On a length, on off and nipping back in off the surface. Lanning defends it out well.
A length ball, outside off and Lanning leaves this one alone.
Back of a length, on middle and angling into the body. Lanning dabs it down on the leg side.
Good-length ball, around off and Beth Mooney taps it through cover-point for a brace.
On off and blocked out by Mooney.
Full and wide, Lanning leans into her cover drive and pierces the off side field. The fielder cuts it out and they come back for the third. Good running.
JAFFA! In that channel around off and just moves away late. Lanning looks to block but the ball zips past the outside edge.
Back of a length, on middle and leg. Mooney hops and tucks it behind square on the leg side for one.
Attempted short ball, down the leg side. Mooney ducks under it.
A length ball, on off and this one keeps a bit low as well. Lanning plays it to mid off.
Length ball, shaping away, outside off. Meg Lanning lets it sail through.
Good-length ball, outside off. Meg Lanning shoulders arms.
Meg Lanning walks out to bat at No.3.

OUT! Dragged on! The experienced Jhulan Goswami strikes early yet again. A good-length ball, outside off. Alyssa Healy goes after it. Healy doesn't move her feet and looks to cut away from her body. The ball keeps a bit low and takes the bottom edge onto the off stump. Healy can't believe it and India Women are ecstatic.
Full and outside off, driven towards cover for a single.
Back of a length, on leg stump. Mooney looks to tuck it away but gets squared up. The ball goes off the glove and towards the off side.
Beaten! On a good-length, around off and this one shapes away nicely. Healy has a poke at it but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Pitched up, on off and Mooney drives it to wide mid off. Mooney is off the mark with the single.
Another length ball, on middle and nipping back in. Mooney blocks it out.
On middle and shaping back in. Mooney nudges it to short mid-wicket.
Fullish ball, around off and shaping away. Healy drives it through covers for a single.
FOUR! On a good length and Alyssa Healy whacks it into the deep mid-wicket fence for a boundary.
Meghna Singh to bowl from the opposite end.
A length ball, on off and going across the left-hander. Beth Mooney gets squared up and gets beaten yet again.
Beauty! Pitched up, around off and just angling away. Mooney pokes at it and gets beaten on the outside edge.
A length ball, on off and Mooney defends it out.

Goswami starts off with a good-length ball, on off. Alyssa Healy taps it to cover-point and sets off for a quick single. Healy and Australia Women are off the mark.
